subject: Consumption fidelity & SLA sensitivity analysis
messages:
From: Dana Cho <dana@heliohealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@heliohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q1 spike + renewal timing

Hi Mina and team,

Quick context: we just finished a feature rollout that drove an unexpected mid-quarter token spike (~2.4x baseline peak) and a handful of latency breaches for some patient-facing flows. We're approaching our contract renewal window (June) and procurement asked that we get a clearer picture of three things before we can move forward:

1) A tight breakdown of token spend by endpoint/prompt family for the last 90 days (we saw big variance week-to-week).
2) The SLA sensitivity — which commit levels keep 99th percentile latency within our target (350ms) given our current model mix and typical batch sizes.
3) An ROI/ops case for a short-term burst/uptick vs committing to a higher flat monthly commit.

Can you share a concise readout and recommend 2 viable renewal paths (one conservative, one aggressive) with the tradeoffs? Also: procurement will want to see any recent redlines and an updated SOW if we alter terms.

Appreciate it — happy to set a 30-min call next week if easier.

Best,
Dana
Director of Product
Helio Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Dana Cho <dana@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q1 spike + renewal timing

Thanks Dana — and sorry to hear about the latency blips. Looping in Karthik (pricing) and Lauren (ops/SLAs). We've pulled preliminary artifacts (attached): Q1 token breakdown by route, a 7-day rolling latency trace, and a short-run simulation that maps commit tiers to projected p99 given your traffic mix.

High-level takeaways (quick):
- The spike concentrated in two prompt families: document-summarization (long tokens) and multi-turn chat for triage. Together they explain ~68% of the excess spend.
- If you keep your current model mix, the p99 grows non-linearly with concurrency; moving to a higher-guaranteed commit reduces queueing and batching variance.
- A 30% uptick bridge (2-month burst credit + short-term uplift) gets you through the next quarter with limited overcommit risk; a 12-month uplift commit reduces unit cost but requires procurement signoff.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik will sketch two priced paths with unit economics and elasticity assumptions.
2) Lauren will validate the SLA sensitivity numbers and recommend operational guardrails (canary settings, client-side backoff).
3) I'll clean the deck and share a one-page comparison for procurement.

Attaching: usage_report_Q1.csv, latency_trace_202704.zip (traces), redlines_v2.pdf (our last SOW changes).

--
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Q1 spike + renewal timing

Following up with two high-level pricing scenarios (numbers are illustrative — will finalize with exact token rates):

Option A — Conservative (short bridge + burst credits)
- Term: 3 months bridge + 6-month evaluation window
- Commit: baseline + 30% burst credit pool (no long-term price change)
- SLA impact: maintains current latency SLOs with a small risk window during sustained spikes
- Economics: effective unit price ~+8% vs current if burst consumed fully

Option B — Aggressive (12-month uplift commit)
- Term: 12 months
- Commit: baseline + 50% uplift committed tokens (discount applied)
- SLA impact: significantly lower queuing risk; p99 headroom improves ~20–30% in our simulations
- Economics: effective unit price ~-12% vs current (after discount) but higher gross exposure if traffic drops

Operational add-ons (recommended):
- Canary window for any model/parameter changes (2 weeks) with automatic rollback on p99 breach.
- Client-specified backoff + server-side throttling for triage chat during peak minutes.

I'll prepare a tight one-pager with numbers by prompt family and elasticity assumptions (ETA: EOD Friday). Mina — want me to include a pro-forma comparing your cost at 60%, 80%, and 100% burst consumption?

—Karthik
Senior Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q1 spike + renewal timing

Thanks all — this is exactly the kind of framing procurement wanted. A couple quick asks before the call: 

- Can you include a short scenario that assumes we shift the document-summarization workload to a smaller-context model (approx -25% token cost) but keep chat on the current models (impact on accuracy? we'll need a short eval).
- For Option B, can procurement see a sample clause to limit overage exposure if usage drops >30% vs commit?

Let's grab 30 minutes next Tue (May 4) to walk through the one-pager and the SOW redlines. Dana and procurement will be on the line.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Dana
Director of Product, Helio Health
